name: ec2-user-data-died-health-ok
description: Diagnose an EC2 instance that boots clean and serves nothing, where every AWS-visible health field reads ok because the instance really is healthy and it is cloud-init that died. Use when: (1) an instance is `running` with `SystemStatus: ok` and `InstanceStatus: ok`, SSH answers, but the ports your user_data was supposed to open are closed, (2) software the bootstrap installs is simply absent and nothing in the console suggests why, (3) you are running any `dnf`/`apt` operation inside user_data on a 512 MB instance (`t4g.nano`, `t3.nano`, `t2.nano`), (4) a bootstrap under `set -e` stopped partway and you cannot tell where, (5) you edited user_data in Terraform and the plan says "will be updated in-place, 0 to destroy" - that plan is a no-op. Two traps: instance status answers "is the VM alive", never "did cloud-init finish", so a green check is not evidence the bootstrap ran; and `user_data` is read only on first boot, so changing it in place changes an API field while the running machine stays exactly as broken.
author: voitta-ai
